notes.title: Update 1.0.1
notes.notes:
Happy new year all.

This update brings two new features:
[list]
[*] Wall-mounted lights
[*] The ability to dig a slightly larger area
[/list]

[h2]Wall-mounted lights[/h2]
These new lights unlock with the same research as required for the existing street lamps.
They might be more suited for indoor areas, as you can attach them to walls (and ceilings).
They require power (cable connections). They themselves can connect up to three cables, similar to the street lamps.

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/f9dc922fd65a73fe2c6a5a464ed9622b18928600.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/53d18b4b2956c5b2f1579fd3f3f04a52c9b406aa.png[/img][/url]

[h2]Digging help[/h2]
When digging through terrain, if you hold shift, it will excavate a rectangular area around the direction you are facing instead of a single block (9 blocks). 
This should make tunneling a little easier. You can of course still use explosive charges as well.

notes.title: Latest branch - 1.0.0
notes.notes:
Note: these changes are available on the 'latest' (experimental) beta branch. To play it, you need to right click the game in steam, choose game properties -> betas -> 'latest' branch. This branch is experimental and not heavily tested yet.


[list]
[*] you can now use right-click to hide the build pattern dialog as well.
[*] small bug fix: while dragging resources, if you close the inventory the drag icon will no longer persist.
[*] rearranged the tutorial sequence a bit and updated some hints and tips entries
[*] machines now show how much power they consume when idle  (if any) .
[*] you now have air control while jumping, under evaluation (updating movement controls can be tricky, if it feels off, too weak or too strong, let me know).
[*] molecular analyzer now also shows consumption and idle consumption.
[*] adjusting the layout of recipe tooltip a bit so we can expand the information more easily. Tooltips now also show how many you or the targeted machine can craft giving the input resources (depends on what inventory is used to craft output).
[*] adjusted collider logic when placing down a new machine. You should now be able to interact with machines immediately regardless of position. Under evaluation. If you experience bumpiness, let me know. If placed very close-by to the player, actual collision is disabled until the player moves away a bit, but interaction is still possible..
[*] rescanned copper, tin and iron ore icons.
[*] craft progress button start fixed.
[*] in game master volume slider still referred to the old slider range (non linear volume control). Fixed that.
[*] the inventory tooltip has been expanded to show more useful information (stacksize, burn value, rp value, analysis level etc).
[/list]


The majority of these additions are in response to player feedback, which is very welcome.
These changes will be integrated into the default game branch at a later time point, once they have been through a bit more testing.

notes.title: Early Access has arrived!
notes.notes:
After working on it for nearly two years, Outpost Engineer is finally out in early access.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/f2f56dc5ab32f3e41520eba1c4575a6ce973ccf7.png[/img]

This release is only the beginning of a long story. The game is perfectly playable as is, there is already a full gameplay loop available including an end goal. 
What will be added during early access is more content, refined recipes and research, some power balancing, UI improvements, more translations, and some new and exciting stuff I have yet to reveal (or even start on... ).
Additionally, feedback from you, the player, will help shape the game further. We already had a small but intense closed beta with the discord community earlier, which proved community feedback is very valuable for sure. A lot of quality of life features were added because of it.
Like a good wine, the game will become even better with age.

Incidentally, it is also my birthday today. ːsteamhappyː
Well, not really a coincidence I must say, but looking back, I do wonder whether it was the greatest idea to release something on a birthday.

Regardless, so happy to get the game out in the open, hope you enjoy!
Do let me know what you think of it. 
An easy way to provide direct feedback on the game itself (features, issues, screenshots) is either by posting in the steam discussions/community or by joining our [url=https://discord.com/invite/c2DrVWp]Discord[/url].


Have fun,
David

notes.title: Devlog #10
notes.notes:
The early access release is very very close (4 days left), so I'm mostly focusing on play testing and some final code cleanup.

But I really can't help myself, I'm still sneaking in some extra goodies.

[h2]Power poles on walls and ceilings[/h2]
The code changes of last week's [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1433470/view/2993184504397337505]explosive charge[/url] addition made it really easy to implement another feature identified by the discord community:
Power poles that you can attach to walls or ceilings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/54dacbdd796d8de3374e09f15121b2c39664b4d4.png[/img]
We already had a small/ floor level power pole. All it took was to enable it to rotate to a surface in a similar way as explosive charges 'latch' to a surface.
If you place them, they will now look at the surrounding 'terrain'. Firstly, if there is solid floor, they will place themselves on floor, else if there are solid walls, they will latch to those walls, and finally, if there is a solid ceiling instead, it will attach to the ceiling.


[h2]Build patterns[/h2]
I also added three new wood patterns to build with, two of them you can see in the below screenshot:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/a57db21a8e3399768177fe68c7d646b408274202.png[/img]

And you can now create steel based blocks once you unlock steel. They might be a bit expensive to build, but they add 5 new metallic patterns for building:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/3486bad0ced9f42605ec98e277dd217117041c8d.png[/img]

Just making sure we have enough creative options here :).


Hope to see you soon in game,
thanks for reading!

notes.title: Devlog #9
notes.notes:
This weeks handles some explosive content!

The game is less than two weeks away from early access. But that is not the only explosive content.

We had a small but very engaging closed beta with the discord community, and one of the suggested features was to add more options to destroy terrain.
Turns out clearing a large floor with a single pickaxe can be somewhat time consuming.

The result is we now have a new option to destroy terrain: An 'explosive charge'.
It is crafted in the assembler (or at the assembly table) by combining one Ammo MK2 with an iron frame.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/d9d100d5d3a672e91485bb472b62a2062abf56a9.png[/img]

When you place it on terrain, it will automatically latch itself to the adjacent surface. After about 5 seconds (during which you can still undeploy the charge), it will destroy a region of 3 by 3 by 3 under it's attachment surface. It will not destroy machines, only terrain that can otherwise also be destroyed by pickaxe:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/d3c9f9cd7fc42c63ea860d056277f93e6f4f524b.gif[/img]

The code to orient the deployed charge will likely be reused later to create small power poles that can attach to walls, or perhaps ceiling/wall lights as well.

As for the coming week, I will mostly be focusing on getting the code in tiptop shape for the early access release on june 8th. 

Hope to see you soon, and thanks for reading!

[list]
[*] Swapped cable station & pole colors. Green is now input.
[*] Fixed an iron block configuration issue.
[*] Steel now only requires one iron, but has a much longer crafting time.
[*] Gave the range dome a small animation and an info box to make it a little bit more clear.
[*] Tweaked the colliders on constructors and inserters a little.
[*] Previously, in the first minute of the game, if you tried to place blocks it could take a little time before the result was seen (due to world loading interfering). Should be immediate now.
[*] Refactored some code for machine update loops.
[*] Worked on a pipe/liquid system, work in progress.
[*] Added smaller version of a floor and wall pattern.
[*] Creep bulbs should no longer spawn on lava.
[*] Fixed combustion generator view.
[*] Mycelium and swamp should be less reflective.
[/list]

notes.title: Devlog #8
notes.notes:
Up until now, supplying machines with resources has been done using one type of inserters, in two variants: Tier 1 copper based, and a tier 2 upgrade which requires iron but has double the speed.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/030277ede739539e80645159bea839793e22e995.gif[/img]

They work fine, but in some situations you have several belts to supply a machine, and you had to get a little creative, puzzle the environment a bit, to get all of them to connect to a machine especially for furnaces.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/99262b60dff3dee6aa84aa265939bcba35fb7d8d.jpg[/img]


The game now also contains a long handed inserter, both a standard version and an MK double speed version.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/df29d45d69ace440c10d0806fced19ebddea9a7c.gif[/img]

These grab resources from one distance further than the regular inserter, effectively allowing you to run two belts in parallel and grab from both.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/8214caaba3cc8646bef152845d07ad4bf1ee6a5c.png[/img]

Double the creativity for supplying, and you can still route resources however you want.
While adding these inserters I also improved the basic pickup animation from the regular inserters a bit, I'm quite happy with the result.


The above screenshots where posted by members of the discord community.

Getting closer to the early access release, hope to welcome you soon!

notes.title: Devlog #7
notes.notes:
Welcome to another devlog!
This week, I'll talk about the newly added tier2 belts.

As discussed in a past [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1433470/view/2916610627120711735]devlog[/url] there are two main modes of transportation in the game right now.
The basic transportation is by conveyor belts.
Bulk cargo transportation, suited for longer distances, can be done with a cable claw system.

[h2]Tier 2 Conveyors and splitters[/h2]
Last week, I have been adding the tier 2 upgrade to the conveyor belt system, which requires iron retrofitting, but doubles the transportation speed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/13a4d95a5f3839c468dfd36b2671935559d1c0c6.gif[/img]

The regular and sloped belts (up and down) now have iron based upgrades.
The vertical and horizontal splitter also have iron based upgrades.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/f327a9768da5d748bd8381b32479fd7178b778eb.png[/img]

Additionally, some quality of life features have been added for building:
[list]
[*] If you click a basic conveyor belt while holding the upgraded version, it automatically updates it in place. The same goes for upgrading splitters.
[*] Like with the basic belts, if you want to build a sloped tier 2 conveyor but don't have any in your inventory, but you have regular tier 2 conveyors in your inventory, you can still build the sloped versions, the regular conveyors are transformed on the fly.
[*] You can also upgrade basic sloped conveyors using regular tier 2 conveyors, they will automatically transform to the correct sloped conveyor.
[/list]

Thanks for reading!

Less than a month before early access release. Exciting!

notes.title: Devlog #6
notes.notes:
One month away from early access release!

The last weeks I have been working hard on a lot of quality of life features (better mouse sensitivity settings, configurable field of view, user interface changes and additions). Also squashed a couple of minor bugs. Most of this came out of (very valuable) feedback from our discord community. We were holding a small scoped closed beta.

But also sneaked in a game addition this week:
Up until now we only had copper containers. These had 4 storage slots, which isn't a lot but convenient enough for many purposes.

This week I'm also adding iron and steel containers.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/030277ede739539e80645159bea839793e22e995.gif[/img]

These unlock once you research iron and steel manufacturing, are made by up-crafting the more basic container versions.
The iron container contains 8 output slots and is made at the assembly table using a copper container and an iron frame.
The steel container contains 16 output slots and is made at the assembly table using an iron container and 4 steel bars.

Similarly to the upgraded inserter versions, I've also made it so you can easily upgrade a lower end container into a higher end container by just clicking on them while holding the higher end container version. The inventory will automatically be upgraded.

There is more, but that will be for another post.

thanks for reading!

You can always follow us on [url=https://discord.com/invite/c2DrVWp]Discord [/url] btw.

notes.title: Devlog #5
notes.notes:
We are now less than two months away before Outpost Engineer releases as early access on Steam.
A large part of my time is currently dedicated to polishing the codebase, doing some test play-throughs, and just making sure everything works.

However, seeing that does not make a very interesting devlog, I figured I talk a bit about the current threat mechanic that is present on the volcanic island.

Spoiler Warning: this is a bit of a [b]spoiler[/b] so skip the text if you want to play without pre-existing knowledge (but on the other hand it is no secret either).

[h2]Pollution[/h2]
Currently, most machines generate pollution, some more than others. 
The world threat comes in the form of an aggressively growing fungal organism that consumes pollution to grow.

The game world is divided into segments called 'chunks' which are 16x16x16 voxels big. 
The pollution slowly accumulates at the chunk level, until it reaches a certain threshold. This pollution can spread to neighboring chunks to some extent.

When the pollution becomes too high however, fungal spores will materialize in the air. They take down a little pollution, and will float around until they hit the terrain.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/15a5e49cfc99add2a253357c75b14fed7fcfa8ee.png[/img]

They are slightly easier to spot at night, but you'll also hear them popping into existence.

[h2]Bulbs[/h2]
When they hit the terrain, they can instantly grow a 'creep bulb' ( some kind of fungal fruiting body) if there isn't one yet in the vicinity and the conditions are favorable.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/52d47d56f326f531af54098ff9a398f49a33b78e.png[/img]

They will also deposit a small amount of 'mycelium', which is the vegetative part of the fungus. This mycelium can be removed with the pickaxe.

Once spawned, Creep bulbs will consume (and hence reduce) pollution to grow. Their growing tactics vary according to the surroundings:
1. If they sense an electrical machine in the vicinity, they will try and grow a tentacle towards it. When they reach the machine, they will sap a small amount of energy from your network.
2. If not, they just grow locally, consuming pollution and converting it into a bulky mycelium body.
3. They may also periodically spawn a toxic cloud, which can damage the player and slow down conveyors temporarily. The cloud cannot pass solid terrain, and will dissipate in time.
4. If pollution is low, they remain dormant.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/8d7261ed21a8a12013efdaac6407cbc914344633.png[/img]

[h2]Defense[/h2]
At first you'll probably need to cleanup the growths manually. You can also take the creep bulbs themselves down.
Once you unlock the research for it however, you can build turrets and produce ammo.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/6ae4611922ae1b2ed079bd191f43ddd81e8f24d7.gif[/img]

Turrets will scan their surroundings for airborne spores and shoot them down. They will also shoot at mycelium growths themselves, slowly chipping them away, and thus cleaning up your factory for you.
The more advanced ammunition can also take down creep bulbs directly.

This mechanic is not meant to overwhelm your base, while providing some pressure it is mostly meant to challenge the player to build more and diversify production, as opposed to creating a game losing situation.
In time, additional gameplay mechanics may be conceived around harvesting these growths. Currently they provide good value for research points.


Thanks for reading!

BTW: If you are interested in participating in a limited closed beta (3 weeks), make sure to check our discord for details (which will be posted very soon).

notes.title: Devlog #4
notes.notes:
Most machines in outpost engineer require power in the form of electricity to operate.
This post highlights the currently implemented ways to generate electricity.

[h2]The Combustion generator[/h2]
The first option you unlock to generate electricity is the combustion generator. It burns coal.
Once you setup automation for it, your first generator will get you good enough power generation for the early game.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/44bc4bbd19ef7267fd3153822524d94f191bd75f.gif[/img]

[h2]Solar panels[/h2]
Late game, once you unlocked silica and circuit boards, you'll unlock solar panels.
Solar panels require no input, but are only active during daytime. During daytime, they follow the inclination of the sun.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/853ca597331547f7c0e3d0dbc65dcc28a832d333.gif[/img]

To expand your electrical storage/capacity, you can also add some accumulators (batteries) to store excess energy.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/ce6fc06c2720cb3060c787f36ef8096871b0aaa9.png[/img]

How much you consume or produce can be consulted by accessing power poles and other electrical systems. The game tracks the last 30 seconds of consumption and production per electrical grid and displays it with some graphs.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/39f33f42065bec9e74a60e6199e2f5b4184e781e.png[/img]

[h2]Particle Cannon[/h2]
The late game goal is to build a particle cannon. It uses energy to charge, and once fully charged can open a stable wormhole portal back to earth.
The time it takes to charge greatly depends on the number of particle accelerators you attach to the cannon. Every added particle accelerator cumulatively decreases charging time but also linearly increases power consumption. You'll need to invest in your energy grid to be able to handle the load.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/36f2495682f56bd9779e00f21bee29da18c336c5.png[/img]


That's it for this post, thank you for reading!

notes.title: Devlog #3
notes.notes:
Outpost Engineer is a crafting and logistics game. As such one fundamental piece of the puzzle is how to get your resources from a to b.
In this post I delve into the current modes of transportation. Mind that the game is still in closed alpha, and more options will likely be added later on.

[h2]Belts and Inserters[/h2]
As in many other automation games, the most basic way of getting a resource from point A to B is by conveyor belt. To load items on and off conveyor belts 'inserters' can be used. These grab resources from containers, machines, or other belts and place them into containers, machines or belts at the opposing side.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/702dfe216632bbb4ee5374d803a3918fcb7dde17.png[/img]

Outpost Engineer is a 3D game, so we need to be able to move resources up and down as well. One way is to use sloped conveyors, which can be crafted whenever you have regular conveyor belts in your inventory.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/4cf0253e895eac5c5ff114cf0bf6e6592829a90a.png[/img]

Once you unlock iron, you will be able to upgrade your inserters to an MK2 version, which has double the speed of the original inserter. Belt upgrade options are also being considered.

[h2]Splitting or Joining belts[/h2]
You can join belts just by pointing the output side to another belt. But there are more advanced options as well which allow you to balance belts to some extent.

The splitter has two input and output sides. It will distribute items in an alternating left/right fashion, unless one side is blocked in which case the other side is prioritized.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/90d9437feb1fdb50de7aba0983b3ea0cea8d1066.png[/img]

Again, this is a 3D game, so we can think in three dimensions for joining belts. There is a vertical splitter variant as well, which has bottom/top input and output sides instead and distributes items accordingly.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/5ffb70e710c25d34aa5d808e0d651c70da10c011.png[/img]

[h2]Advanced transportation: Cable claw[/h2]
Once steel is unlocked, a new transportation method becomes available, more suited for long distance transportation.
Resources are packed into crates, and loaded/unloaded at cable stations. When there is a demand (and there is a path by cable), a cable claw will transport such a crate to the target destination.
Cable transportation uses a network of connected poles, and spawns crates only when there is a demand.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/703314d385ce3bc718041da4392c40811d333659.png[/img]

These are the current modes of transportation. The game is still in closed alpha, and as times goes on I'm sure variants will be added.

Hope you enjoyed this post

Greetings,
David

notes.title: Devlog #2
notes.notes:
Hello All,

A progress report. I've been mostly working on integrating some mid game products and resources:

[h2]Iron[/h2]
Iron ore patches can only be found in the sandstone biome, which is a biome consisting of arches and hills, every island has one.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/03600dae3bb20238688906a10ebd50700142a3b9.png[/img]

Once unlocked, iron ore can be processed into iron rods iron frames. And later in the game, also steel beams.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/a7406385369eb24e57ea457bc05ccda835aebdad.png[/img]

[h2]Silica[/h2]
Silica shards are created by smelting sand in a furnace. They will be used to create lamp posts and, later in the game, electronic circuits.
Large products such as these lamp posts are transported as crates. It would be very impractical to try and transport them on belts when they are fully assembled.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/2ecaae8ede6d15ec10b183eaf9e1203286c563e7.png[/img]

[h2]Lithium electrolyzer[/h2]
Another advanced resource is lithium, which will primarily be used to build batteries.
I wanted a bit more variety in extraction mechanisms. In the real world, lithium is often extracted from seawater. Seeing in game we are on an island, I decided to create the first structure that requires a salt water placement to operate, the lithium electrolyzer.
When building, you'll only be allowed to build this structure in shallow salt water.
As a mid game structure, it does consume quite a lot of power.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/1a2d8bebc5d30bf98125871bde77f14532567549.gif[/img]




Thanks for reading!

notes.title: DevLog #1
notes.notes:
Hi

This is my first devlog about Outpost Engineer. As such I'd like to introduce myself.

[h2]About me[/h2]
I am the solo developer of Outpost Engineer.
I've been a gamer for a long time. I'm also a software developer. I've dabbled with many smaller projects in the past, and started to create this game because I wanted to create something I enjoy playing,
and wanted to finally combine my skills as a developer with something I love doing.
I am heavily inspired by other great factory automation games and base building games such as factorio, satisfactory, fortresscraft evolved, oxygen not included and more.

[h2]Current Status[/h2]
I've been working on Outpost Engineer for a while now, and as such, the foundations of the game are already there.

[h3]Gameplay[/h3]
As for gameplay, I have currently implemented what you could call the first tier of processing and factory automation:
Smelting tin, copper and bronze.
Creating products from bars, such as copper wires, bronze gears, tin plates.
A transportation system, consisting of conveyor belts and splitters. Inserters can pull resources from belts or containers and pass them to machines.
An electrical grid system, and an electricity generator.
Constructors and Assemblers which can take products and make more complex products (such as more conveyor belts, inserters, etc).
A research system, based on analyzing resources, generating datacubes, and communicating those back to earth, in exchange for blueprints.
A day and night system, and torches and streetlights to illuminate the darkness.

[h3]Tech[/h3]
The voxel based rendering of the terrain is 'chunk' based and works smoothly. I'm using a home grown shader to render the terrain. It uses barycentric coordinates to blend voxels of different types at the edges.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/d51e7150b7dd178b7aa5b9763be85c7911e2cfe5.png[/img]
Image: The wall is made out of three types of wood patterns. The lamppost is plain concrete. The floor is built from concrete tiles.

The textures are stored in texture arrays, allowing me to add new textures for terrain and structures as I see fit. I currently have about 80 different texture/voxel types, which include several variants of concrete, wood, and metal textures.
I'm going for a bit of a steampunk and concrete look for the game (at least the factory part). I plan an adding more textures as I go on.
The rendering uses a marching cubes algorithm for the voxels, which means you won't be seeing block worlds.
The terrain is, depending on the voxel type, smooth (grasslands, hills and mountains) or chunky (when you build walls and floors for example).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/41f40e92c81c2e7aaaeeffc1d20907df5749daf4.png[/img]
Image: A manually built structure, at night. Some copper and tin metal panels included.

All 3d assets (products, machines, ...) are currently also built out of voxel models.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38931510/f59524974f1d011f08a697873612525ca73e6d25.png[/img]
Image: Some bronze gears, copper wires and tin plates.

The user interface is largely functional, with a main menu, mappable keys, configuration settings and detail pages on selected machines, crafting stations and more.

A save system is in place. Save files will be per world, and saving is done automatically (when you exit, when changes happen to the terrain, and at regular intervals).

[h2]Plans[/h2]
While the current game is already somewhat playable and enjoyable I have a lot more plans though. I also have more polishing to do before I can release the game.
My current expectation is to be able to release the game, as early access, in  June 2021.

More devlogs will follow.
You can also find me on Twitter (see external links) where I regularly post screenshots and small videos about the development progress.


Thank you for reading!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1433470/Outpost_Engineer/
